findings.title: Invalid input now returns None instead of raising ValueError
findings.detail: The added `except Exception: return None` converts every parsing failure into a silent None result. The required contract is `parse_value` returns `int(value)` and invalid strings raise ValueError. With this patch, `parse_value('abc')` swallows the ValueError from `int('abc')` and returns None, so callers can no longer distinguish invalid input from a legitimate missing value, and the contract-breaking behavior is introduced rather than fixed. The deleted `return int(value)` (old line 2) was already contract-compliant.

findings.title: Blanket `except Exception` hides non-parsing errors and programming faults
findings.detail: `except Exception` is broader than the ValueError the contract expects. Any exception raised inside `int(value)` — including TypeError for unexpected argument types (e.g. None) or errors from a custom `__int__`/`__index__` implementation — is silently mapped to None. This masks genuine bugs and prevents callers from seeing failures they previously would have received from the unguarded `int(value)` call.

unbounded_retry.summary: The patch replaces a direct fetch call with an unconditional `while True` retry that catches every `Exception` and immediately continues. This inverts the required behavior: instead of propagating a persistent dependency failure, `load` spins forever, and it also masks non-transient/programming errors as retryable. No backoff, attempt cap, or re-raise is present in the supplied diff.

findings.title: Unbounded retry loop hangs on persistent dependency failure
findings.detail: The added `while True:` loop retries `fetch()` forever. If the dependency fails persistently (the exact scenario in the required behavior), `load` never returns and never propagates the error: each failure hits `except Exception: continue` and control returns to the top of the loop with no attempt counter, deadline, or backoff. This replaces the deleted `return fetch()` (old line 2), which was the only path that surfaced the failure to the caller, so the contract 'propagate persistent dependency failure without hanging or spinning indefinitely' is violated and callers block/burn CPU indefinitely.

findings.title: Blanket exception handling converts non-transient errors into infinite retries
findings.detail: `except Exception:` captures every error type raised by `fetch()`, including deterministic programming errors such as `TypeError`, `AttributeError`, or validation failures that can never succeed on retry. Because the handler only executes `continue`, these errors are silently swallowed and the call is retried forever rather than raised to the caller. This hides defects and removes the fail-fast behavior of the deleted `return fetch()` line, so a permanently broken `fetch` produces an unkillable spin loop instead of a diagnosable exception.

removed_permission_check.summary: The patch removes the authorization guard from read_secret, so the explicitly required PermissionError for unauthorized callers is gone; this is a direct regression of a safety check and fails the stated required behavior.

findings.title: Authorization check deleted; read_secret(False) no longer raises PermissionError

With the guard removed, any caller passing authorized=False reaches the return statement and obtains the secret instead of raising PermissionError, violating the required behavior "read_secret(False) must raise PermissionError; secret is defined elsewhere. Preserve authorization." Unauthorized access to the secret is now possible, so the original root cause is not merely unresolved but newly introduced.
